claims.title: How do all the translated forms acquire a common level and bound?
claims.hypotheses: Two auxiliary split places over ℓ have different primes below them in the real subfield. The original weight form is fixed by the specified restricted level.
claims.statement: A common compact finite level admits an equivariant label. Correcting the original form by this label gives translated forms fixed by that level and uniformly bounded in the original integral frame.

claims.title: Why does the sum over local pieces define a finite family of automorphic forms?
claims.hypotheses: The ambient unitary group is definite. The compact level, translated forms and local indicator polynomials are chosen for the original algebraic weight.
claims.statement: For each dominant target the finite sum is an automorphic family with common level, two matrix covariance laws, finite-dimensional span and the required one-sided bounds on circle exponents.

claims.title: How can one decompose every member of the family at once?
claims.hypotheses: A two-matrix family of automorphic functions on the definite unitary group has finite-dimensional span, fixed level and two circle constraints.
claims.statement: One finite direct sum of irreducible automorphic representations contains every family value. The projected families obey the same covariance, level and separate circle constraints.

claims.title: Why are the highest-weight partial sums bounded on both sides?
claims.hypotheses: A projected family is nonzero in an automorphic constituent having weight κ. The full-circle upper estimate and the separate lower estimate on the identity slice hold.
claims.statement: At each k, the difference of the partial sums of the realized and target weights is at most d in absolute value. Each individual weight entry consequently differs by at most 2d.

claims.title: Which powers can occur when a weight is restricted to one circle?
claims.hypotheses: The rank is positive and κ is a dominant list of integers. The first k coordinates are scaled by a point of the unit circle.
claims.statement: Every coefficient of the weight module has Laurent exponents between k times the last weight and the sum of the first k weights. The highest-weight vector attains the upper endpoint. Upper triangular matrices act on it by the highest-weight character.

claims.title: Can a specified nonzero vector be detected at the chosen embedding?
claims.hypotheses: An irreducible group representation contains a given irreducible type on a subgroup. Each group element is a product of a subgroup element and an element centralizing that subgroup.
claims.statement: Any specified nonzero vector admits an equivariant linear map to the type that is nonzero on this vector.

claims.title: Which parts of the original weight survive the projection?
claims.hypotheses: The projected family is nonzero, the group is definite, and only one archimedean factor acts on the matrix arguments.
claims.statement: At every other archimedean place the constituent has the original weight at both embedding labels. A nonzero value of the family supplies a vector fixed by the required finite level.
